text:
maria_cs: FYI incoming request from Helios Aerospace — they want Redwood to onboard a custom 'telemetry-parser-7b' model to parse high-frequency flight telemetry and output normalized events. Asking for private deployment (VPC + on-prem ingestion gateway) and HSM for keys. ,
ben_se: Got it. Do we have the model artifact URL or is this a model-hosting request? :thinking_face:
maria_cs: Customer says they will supply a PyTorch .pt and tokenizer files. They also want us to run safety/eval checks before enabling traffic. Timeline: pilot in 3 weeks. ,
sam_qa: We should capture expected QPS and latency SLO. Telemetry tends to be bursty. Maria — did they provide throughput numbers?
maria_cs: Initial ask: ingest ~500 req/s bursts, typical 50 req/s. Latency SLO 200ms p50 on inference, willing to accept higher p95 if we batch. They want vector embeddings for anomaly tagging too.
ben_se: For 7B sized model on Dedicated, 200ms p50 is tight at that QPS. Options: quantize + batching + cold KV cache warming. Also ask if they need real-time tail latency <200ms or just p50. ,
maria_cs: Customer clarified: p50 200ms is target for event-to-label end-to-end, they can accept p95 up to 1.2s during bursts. Key constraint: flight data is sensitive — must stay in their VPC, long-term storage on their S3, HSM for in-transit key ops.
leo_legal: Flag: Helios mentioned export restrictions in their intake. Need legal review for restricted tech and whether model contains any controlled IP. I'll start intake questionnaire.
sam_qa: Proposed eval plan: 1) smoke parse test (1000 records) 2) accuracy on labeled parse set (precision/recall) 3) latency profile under bursty load using our load harness 4) safety checks for hallucination on edge telemetry. I can draft a checklist.
maria_cs: Thanks. Also customer asked about our rollback/fallback behavior — if model fails, they want automatic fallback to a rules-based parser (their existing system) and alerting routed to Helios support channel.
ben_se: Technically we can wire a canary + fallback route. Need to confirm model output schema so rules parser consumes same field names. Ask them for schema sample and at least 2 weeks of representative telemetry for caches/batching calibration.
opsbot: deploy-bot notice: Created tracker ticket CS-HELIOS-102 in customer-success board.
maria_cs: I'll request the schema and the sample dataset today. Sam — can you draft the eval harness and perf tests? Ben — can you propose Dedicated sizing and quantization recommendations? Leo will handle the legal intake.
sam_qa: On it. I'll attach an example harness snippet for them to run locally or share dataset: ```python
# simple load harness
from loadgen import BurstRunner
r = BurstRunner(model_endpoint="placeholder", qps=500, burst_profile=[500,200,50])
r.run(duration=600)
```
ben_se: Draft sizing: start with 2x A100-80 per pool for 7B float32; prefer int8/4-bit quantization with Redwood Optimize — that should cut GPU mem and improve p50. I'll outline fallback routing config.
leo_legal: Started the intake. Maria — loop in Helios security contact and provide the data handling checklist I just posted. We may need an NDA addendum and DFARS/ITAR screening; marking renewal risk if they require long-term on-prem maintenance.
maria_cs: Great. I'll update the Helios ticket and ask for dataset + schema + security contact. Expect an update by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
ben_se: cool. tagging @eng-runtime for awareness during sizing conversation.
sam_qa: I'll prep the eval doc and share by tomorrow noon.
maria_cs: Thanks team — keeping this thread as the single source. Will post customer replies here.
